# Volume 2 — XXVII An Afternoon at the Stone House

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

“Nell, where are you headed, so finely clad?” Robin inquired. “That dress makes you look stunning.”
{: #nw-v02-c27-p0000 }

Nell had descended to the evening meal wearing a fresh gown of faint green muslin . . . the initial hue she had adopted following Obed’s passing. It suited her flawlessly, accentuating every fragile, blossom-like tone of her complexion along with the luster and sheen of her locks.
{: #nw-v02-c27-p0001 }

“Robin, I have repeatedly instructed you to avoid using that word,” she admonished. “Echo Cottage is where I am heading.”
{: #nw-v02-c27-p0002 }

“Take me with you,” Robin begged.
{: #nw-v02-c27-p0003 }

“If I were traveling by car, I would bring you. However, I plan to go on foot, a distance too great for legs belonging to an eight-year-old. Furthermore, Cedric will accompany me, and I suspect his presence does not bring you pleasure.”
{: #nw-v02-c27-p0004 }

“Oh, my liking for Cedric has grown considerably,” Robin stated, commencing a fierce assault upon his dessert. “His superior virtue isn't as bothersome to me now that my own has improved quite a bit. Provided I maintain my progress, I will eventually equal him, in legs as well as in virtue. Furthermore, Cedric treats us second-primer schoolboys very kindly. He prevents the remaining older pupils from bothering us, and he teaches us numerous games.”
{: #nw-v02-c27-p0005 }

“Why did Cedric drop into the stream at lunchtime yesterday?” Nell inquired. “Upon seeing him on the playground, he was so soaked that I dispatched him straight home to get dressed before I could learn the reason.”
{: #nw-v02-c27-p0006 }

“Indeed, it happened partly by zacksident,” Robin clarified. “Though he intentionally dipped his head, the remainder of his body tumbled in zacksidentally. All of us were gathered by the brook, and Prillie Rogerson grew angry with Cedric over some matter . . . she possesses a really mean and terrible nature regardless, even if she IS attractive . . . and claimed his hair was wrapped in curl rags by his grandmother each evening. I suppose Cedric would not have cared about her remark, except Gracie Pullen giggled, which caused Cedric to turn extremely red, since Gracie is his sweetheart, as you are aware. He is completely smitten with her . . . presenting her with blooms and transporting her schoolbooks all the way to the shore road. Turning as crimson as a beet, he declared that his grandmother performed no such act and that he possessed natural curls from birth. Following that, he reclined upon the edge and plunged his head straight into the spring so they could see. Oh, it failed to be the drinking spring we use . . .” noticing a expression of horror across Thirza’s face . . . “it was the smaller one further down the stream. However, the edge is extremely slick, causing Cedric to slide completely inside. I assure you he generated a grand splash. Oh, Nell, Nell, I failed to intend to speak those words . . . they merely escaped me prior to my thinking. He created a magnificent splash. Nevertheless, he appeared utterly comical as he dragged himself out, entirely drenched and covered in mud. The female children giggled even harder, yet Gracie refrained from laughing. She appeared regretful. Gracie is a lovely female child, though she possesses a turned-up nose. Once I grow sufficiently old to possess a sweetheart, I shall refuse to choose one featuring a turned-up nose . . . I shall select one possessing an attractive nose like yours, Nell.”
{: #nw-v02-c27-p0007 }

“A youth who gets pudding syrup so thoroughly scrambled across his features during mealtime is sure to be ignored by every young woman,” Thirza declared strictly.
{: #nw-v02-c27-p0008 }

“However, I will clean my face prior to going courting,” Robin argued, attempting to make things better as he dragged the back of his hand across the smudges. “Furthermore, I will clean behind my ears as well, even if nobody tells me. Thirza, I remembered to do it this morning. My forgetting happens not nearly as frequently as it used to. Nevertheless . . .” Robin then gave a sigh . . . “a person has such a great number of corners that keeping track of every single one is terribly difficult. Oh well, provided I am unable to visit Miss Rosalind’s, I will head over to visit Mrs. Pettifer instead. I am telling you, Mrs. Pettifer is a tremendously pleasant woman. Inside her pantry, she maintains a cookie jar specifically for young boys, and whenever she has prepared a plum cake, she invariably presents me with the remnants scraped from the pan. As you can understand, a large quantity of plums remain attached to the sides. Mr. Pettifer was invariably a pleasant man, yet his pleasantness has doubled ever since he remarried. It seems to me that marrying causes people to become kinder. Thirza, for what reason do you not get married? I am curious to learn.”
{: #nw-v02-c27-p0009 }

Being unwed had not ever proved to be a tender subject for Thirza, hence she replied pleasantly, trading a meaningful glance with Nell, saying that she presumed no one desired to marry her.
{: #nw-v02-c27-p0010 }

“However, perhaps you didn't ever request that anyone take you,” Robin objected.
{: #nw-v02-c27-p0011 }

“Oh, Robin,” Lucy said with primness, startled into making a remark without prior address, “the asking has to be done by the men.”
{: #nw-v02-c27-p0012 }

“I can’t understand why they must continually act this way,” muttered Robin. “It appears to me that the men bear the entire burden in this life. May I take another portion of pudding, Thirza?”
{: #nw-v02-c27-p0013 }

“As much as was beneficial for you has been served,” Thirza remarked; nevertheless, she provided him with an average additional portion.
{: #nw-v02-c27-p0014 }

“I would be glad if individuals were able to subsist on pudding. What prevents them, Thirza? It is something I desire to understand.”
{: #nw-v02-c27-p0015 }

“For the reason that they would before long grow weary of it.”
{: #nw-v02-c27-p0016 }

“I want to test that on my own,” stated doubting Robin. “However, I suppose getting pudding exclusively on fish and visitor days surpasses having it never. At Milty Gammon’s, they do not ever get any. Milty remarks that whenever visitors arrive, his mother serves them cheese and divides it personally . . . a single small portion per person and an extra one for politeness.”
{: #nw-v02-c27-p0017 }

“If Milty Gammon speaks about his mother in such a manner, you certainly do not need to echo his words,” Thirza said sternly.
{: #nw-v02-c27-p0018 }

“Bless my soul,” . . . Robin had learned this phrase from Mr. Pettifer and employed it with enormous enthusiasm . . . “Milty intended it to be a compelment. He’s terrible proud of his mother, because people claim she could eke out a living on a rock.”
{: #nw-v02-c27-p0019 }

“I . . . I imagine those troublesome hens have gotten into my pansy bed once more,” remarked Thirza, standing up and exiting in a rush.
{: #nw-v02-c27-p0020 }

The maligned chickens were not anywhere close to the patch of pansies, a spot Thirza failed to so much as look toward. Rather than looking there, she took a seat upon the cellar door, laughing continuously to the point that she felt embarrassed by her own behavior.
{: #nw-v02-c27-p0021 }

Upon arriving at the stone house that afternoon, Nell and Cedric discovered Miss Rosalind and Belinda the Fourth working in the garden, where they were weeding, raking, clipping, and trimming with desperate intensity. Miss Rosalind herself, looking joyful and lovely amid the frills and laces she cherished, set down her shears and rushed with delight to greet her visitors, as Belinda the Fourth offered a cheerful grin.
{: #nw-v02-c27-p0022 }

“Greetings, Nell. It occurred to me that today would bring your arrival. It delivered you because the afternoon is where you belong. Items that are meant for one another inevitably unite. If folks were simply aware of that fact, how much effort it would spare them. They remain ignorant, however . . . and consequently expend precious vitality upending everything to unite items that are mismatched. As for you, Cedric . . . well, you have gotten bigger! Since your previous visit, your height has increased by half a head.”
{: #nw-v02-c27-p0023 }

“Yes, I’ve started growing like pigweed overnight, just as Mrs. Sowerby remarks,” Cedric stated, completely charmed by the situation. “Grandma believes the porridge is finally doing its work. Maybe that's true. Goodness knows . . .” Cedric let out a profound sigh . . . “the amount I’ve consumed is sufficient to cause anyone to grow. Now that I’ve started, I really hope to continue until my height equals father’s. He stands at six feet, as you are aware, Miss Rosalind.”
{: #nw-v02-c27-p0024 }

Indeed, Miss Rosalind was aware; the color on her lovely cheeks grew slightly darker; holding Cedric’s hand in one of hers and Nell’s in the other, she proceeded toward the house without speaking.
{: #nw-v02-c27-p0025 }

“Is it a good day for the echoes, Miss Rosalind?” Cedric asked in an anxious manner. Because the day of his initial visit had possessed too much wind for echoes, Cedric had experienced great disappointment.
{: #nw-v02-c27-p0026 }

“Indeed, it is simply the finest sort of day,” replied Miss Rosalind, coming out of her thoughts. “However, everyone will partake in some food beforehand. You two individuals surely became famished during your long trek back through those beechwood trees, whereas Belinda the Fourth and I possess the ability to dine at any given time . . . our appetites are delightfully accommodating. Thus, we shall simply plunder the larder. By good fortune, it is wonderfully stocked. A hunch told me that visitors would arrive today, so Belinda the Fourth and I made ready.”
{: #nw-v02-c27-p0027 }

“It seems to me that you are among those who keep delightful treats stocked in their pantry,” Cedric stated. “Grandma is similar in that way. However, having snacks outside of mealtimes is something she disapproves of. I am pondering,” he continued in a thoughtful tone, “whether I should consume them when I am not at home, knowing full well she disapproves.”
{: #nw-v02-c27-p0028 }

“Oh, after a long walk, I doubt she would mind. That alters things,” stated Miss Rosalind, who shared entertained looks with Nell across the brown curls of Cedric. “I imagine that light bites are terribly bad for one's health. That explains our frequent consumption of them at Echo Cottage. Belinda the Fourth and I live by flouting every established rule regarding food. Daytime or nighttime, whenever the mood strikes, we consume all manner of heavy foods; yet we thrive like green bay trees. Reforming our ways is our constant intention. Should we come across a newspaper piece cautioning about a treat we enjoy, we snip it out and attach it to the kitchen wall for memory's sake. Somehow, though, we never manage to . . . until that exact food has already been consumed. We have not been slain by anything so far; nevertheless, following pre-bedtime helpings of doughnuts, mince pie, and fruit cake, Belinda the Fourth has been observed experiencing nightmares.”
{: #nw-v02-c27-p0029 }

“Grandma permits me to drink a glass of milk and eat a piece of bread and butter prior to going to sleep; and when it is Sunday night she spreads jam on the bread,” Cedric said. “Therefore I am consistently pleased when Sunday night arrives . . . owing to several reasons. Sunday passes as a very lengthy day on the shore road. Grandma states that it feels far too brief for her and that father did not ever consider Sundays tedious when he was a small boy. It would not appear quite as long if I was able to converse with my rock people, yet I do not ever do that since Grandma disapproves of it on Sundays. I do a lot of thinking; however, I fear that my thoughts prove worldly. Grandma states that we ought to solely think religious thoughts on Sundays. However, teacher here mentioned one time that all truly lovely thoughts were religious, regardless of what they concerned, or which day they occurred to us on. However, I am certain Grandma believes that sermons and Sunday School lessons represent the sole matters concerning which a person can think genuinely religious thoughts. And whenever a disagreement in opinion occurs between Grandma and teacher, I am uncertain how to act. Within my heart” . . . Cedric placed his hand upon his chest and lifted exceptionally earnest blue eyes toward Miss Rosalind’s instantly understanding face . . . “I side with teacher. Yet then, as you observe, Grandma raised father according to her method and turned him into a brilliant success; whereas teacher has not raised anyone up to this point, although she assists regarding Robin and Lucy. Still, one is unable to know how those two will develop until they reach adulthood. Thus at times I sense that following Grandma’s views might be safer.”
{: #nw-v02-c27-p0030 }

“It would, in my opinion,” Nell gravely concurred. “Regardless, I venture that should your Grandma and I both get to the core of our actual meaning, despite our distinct manners of articulating it, we would discover that we both intended virtually identical things. You ought to follow her manner of articulating it, as experience has produced it. Until we witness the ultimate outcome of the twins, we must hold off on confirming whether my manner is just as effective.” Following their noon meal, their return to the garden occurred, where Cedric was introduced to the echoes, experiencing awe and pleasure, whereas Nell and Miss Rosalind took seats upon the stone bench beneath the poplar tree to converse.
{: #nw-v02-c27-p0031 }

“So you are going away in the fall?” Miss Rosalind inquired with sadness. “For your sake, Nell, I ought to be glad . . . but I am dreadfully and selfishly grieved. I will miss you terribly. Oh, at times, it seems to me that making friends serves no purpose. After a bit, they merely depart from your life, leaving behind an ache that exceeds the void existing before their arrival.”
{: #nw-v02-c27-p0032 }

“Miss Eliza Pullen might utter such a remark, but Miss Rosalind certainly would not,” Nell remarked. “Emptiness is the absolute worst thing . . . and my departure from your existence is not happening. Letters and vacations do exist, after all. My dear, you appear somewhat pale and exhausted, I fear.”
{: #nw-v02-c27-p0033 }

“Oh . . . hoo . . . hoo . . . hoo,” proceeded Cedric upon the embankment, where he had been persistently producing sounds . . . not every one of them harmonious as they were produced, but all of them returning converted into the actual gold and silver of acoustics by the sprite enchanters across the stream. Miss Rosalind performed an irritated gesture using her attractive hands.
{: #nw-v02-c27-p0034 }

“Everything has simply made me weary . . . even the reverberations. My existence contains nothing except reverberations . . . reverberations of vanished expectations, visions, and delights. Mocking as they are, they remain lovely. Oh Nell, speaking in this manner while hosting a visitor is dreadful on my part. The problem is merely my advancing age, which does not suit me. Reaching sixty will surely find me terribly ill-tempered. A series of blue pills, however, might be the sole remedy I require.” Right then, Belinda the Fourth, who was nowhere to be seen following the midday meal, came back and declared that early strawberries turned the northeast section of Mr. John Kimball’s field red, asking whether Miss Harcourt would care to gather a few.
{: #nw-v02-c27-p0035 }

“Strawberries early for tea!” cried Miss Rosalind. “Oh, my age isn't what I believed . . . and I do not require one blue pill! Girls, after returning with your strawberries we will take tea in this spot beneath the silver poplar. It will be fully prepared by me for you with cream grown at home.”
{: #nw-v02-c27-p0036 }

Nell and Belinda the Fourth consequently made their way back to the pasture belonging to Mr. Kimball, a verdant, secluded spot where the air possessed a velvet-like softness, a fragrance resembling a bed of violets, and an amber goldenness.
{: #nw-v02-c27-p0037 }

“Oh, is it not fresh and sweet in this back area?” Nell whispered. “It simply feels to me like I am absorbing the sunlight.”
{: #nw-v02-c27-p0038 }

“Yes, ma’am, so do I. That’s just exactly how I feel too, ma’am,” concurred Belinda the Fourth, who would have uttered the selfsame words had Nell observed that she felt similar to a pelican of the wilderness. Continual upon Nell's visits to Echo Cottage, Belinda the Fourth ascended to her small chamber above the kitchen and attempted in front of her mirror to converse and appear and walk in the manner of Nell. Belinda was never able to convince herself that she fully accomplished it; nevertheless, practice makes perfect, just as Belinda had been taught at school, and she tenderly trusted that eventually she could acquire the art of that delicate raising of chin, that swift, starry beaming of eyes, that manner of strolling as though one were a branch bending in the breeze. Observing Nell made it appear quite simple. Belinda the Fourth held Nell in total admiration. This was not because she considered her so extremely good-looking. Isolde Pembroke’s attractiveness of red cheek and dark ringlets suited Belinda the Fourth’s preference far better than Nell’s moonlight appeal of radiant gray eyes and the fair, constantly shifting roses of her cheeks.
{: #nw-v02-c27-p0039 }

“However, I would prefer looking like you to being attractive,” she expressed to Nell in all honesty.
{: #nw-v02-c27-p0040 }

Nell chuckled, drank in the sweetness of the praise, and discarded its sharp bite. Mixed compliments were something she had grown accustomed to receiving. Concerning Nell’s appearance, the general consensus was always divided. Individuals who expected a handsome woman upon meeting her felt let down. Individuals who expected an unattractive woman saw her and questioned the vision of others. As for Nell herself, she would not ever accept that she possessed any beauty whatsoever. Gazing into the mirror, the only thing she noticed was a small, white face bearing seven freckles upon its nose. The glass failed to show her the subtle, constantly shifting emotion that passed across her countenance such as a pinkish, glowing light, or the alluring mix of reverie and amusement that shifted within her large eyes.
{: #nw-v02-c27-p0041 }

Although Nell lacked beauty according to any rigid definition of the term, she had an elusive grace and notable air that granted observers a delightful feeling of contentment when viewing her gently curved youth, which was filled with deeply sensed capacities. People who were most familiar with Nell experienced, despite not consciously recognizing it, a sense that her most compelling feature was the vibe of potentiality that enveloped her. . . the capacity for upcoming growth contained within her. It appeared as though she moved within an aura of events on the verge of occurring.
{: #nw-v02-c27-p0042 }

While they gathered, Belinda the Fourth shared with Nell her anxieties concerning Miss Rosalind. The compassionate young servant was genuinely troubled about the state of her cherished mistress.
{: #nw-v02-c27-p0043 }

“Miss Rosalind is sick, Miss Harcourt, ma’am. Though she keeps it to herself, I am certain of it. For a great while now, she has been acting strangely, ma’am . . . ever since the previous time that Cedric and you visited here as one. That evening, I am positive she took a chill, ma’am. Following the departure of him and you, she stepped outside and strolled around the garden well past nightfall, wearing merely a small shawl. Snow lay thick upon the paths, and I am convinced she caught a cold, ma’am. From that moment onward, I have seen her looking weary and lonely. Nothing appears to hold her attention, ma’am. She does not play at having guests, nor does she dress up for them, nor any such thing, ma’am. Only upon your arrival does she appear to brighten up slightly. And indicating the most terrible omen, Miss Harcourt, ma’am . . .” Belinda the Fourth dropped her tone to a whisper, as though she intended to reveal a truly bizarre and horrific condition . . . “when I shatter items now, she fails to grow angry. Why, Miss Harcourt, ma’am, I shattered her green and yaller bowl yesterday, the one that continuously rested atop the bookcase. It was brought over from England by her grandmother, and Miss Rosalind treasured it immensely. As I was wiping it with utmost caution, Miss Harcourt, ma’am, it slipped right out, in that manner, before my hands could catch it, and smashed into roughly forty millyun fragments. I swear I felt terribly grieved and frightened. It was my expectation that Miss Rosalind would reprimand me terribly, ma’am; and I would have preferred a scolding over her actual reaction. Coming into the room, she barely glanced at the mess and remarked, ‘It doesn’t matter, Belinda. Gather the fragments and discard them.’ Spoken precisely like that, Miss Harcourt, ma’am . . . ‘gather the fragments and discard them,’ precisely as though it lacked value as her grandmother’s bowl from England. Oh, her health is failing, and it makes me feel terrible. Except for me, there is no one else to care for her.”
{: #nw-v02-c27-p0044 }

Tears filled Belinda the Fourth’s eyes. Comfortingly, Nell stroked the small brown paw that was grasping the damaged pink cup.
{: #nw-v02-c27-p0045 }

“Belinda, it seems to me that Miss Rosalind requires a change of scenery. Her time spent here in solitude is far too great. Is there no way we can persuade her to take a short journey?”
{: #nw-v02-c27-p0046 }

Belinda, wearing a headpiece filled with wild ribbons, shook her head in a crestfallen manner.
{: #nw-v02-c27-p0047 }

“I do not believe that is the case, Miss Harcourt, ma’am. Visiting is something Miss Rosalind detests. Three relatives are all she ever pays visits to, and according to her, those calls are made strictly out of family duty. Upon her return after the most recent occasion, she declared that she would no longer go on visits due to family duty. ‘Belinda, I’ve returned home enamored with solitude,’ she tells me, ‘and my wish is to never wander away from my own vine and fig tree again. An effort is made so earnestly by my relatives to turn me into an old woman, and it impacts me poorly.’ Precisely in those words, Miss Harcourt, ma’am. ‘It impacts me very poorly.’ Therefore, I doubt that encouraging her to go on a visit would accomplish anything.”
{: #nw-v02-c27-p0048 }

“We have to discover what is possible,” declared Nell firmly, while placing the final berry she could fit into her pink cup. “The moment my vacation begins, I will travel over to stay an entire week alongside you. Every day we will enjoy a picnic, imagine various engaging scenarios, and try to brighten Miss Rosalind's spirits.”
{: #nw-v02-c27-p0049 }

“That will be the very thing, Miss Harcourt, ma’am,” Belinda the Fourth uttered delightedly. For Miss Rosalind’s benefit, as well as her own, she felt happy. Having an entire week to observe Nell continuously, she would certainly manage to discover how to carry herself and act just like her.
{: #nw-v02-c27-p0050 }

Upon the girls' return to Echo Cottage, Miss Rosalind and Cedric had already moved the small, square kitchen table into the garden and prepared the complete spread for tea. Under an expansive blue sky layered with soft, white clouds, and amid the elongated shadows of the rustling, murmuring forest, no meal had ever seemed more delectable than those strawberries and cream. Once tea concluded, Nell assisted Belinda with the dishwashing inside the kitchen, whereas Miss Rosalind took a seat on the stone bench beside Cedric to learn everything concerning his rock people. This gentle Miss Rosalind listened attentively, yet right at the very end, Cedric noticed that her attention regarding the Twin Sailors had abruptly vanished.
{: #nw-v02-c27-p0051 }

“Miss Rosalind, what makes you gaze upon me in such a manner?” he inquired with seriousness.
{: #nw-v02-c27-p0052 }

“Cedric, how do I look?”
{: #nw-v02-c27-p0053 }

“As though your gaze passes right through my form to a person I bring to your memory,” remarked Cedric, whose periodic bursts of eerie perception rendered the keeping of confidences somewhat risky whenever he was around.
{: #nw-v02-c27-p0054 }

“Indeed, you remind me of an acquaintance from my past,” Miss Rosalind said in a dreamy tone.
{: #nw-v02-c27-p0055 }

“Back in your youth?”
{: #nw-v02-c27-p0056 }

“Indeed, back in my youth. Is it your impression that I am quite aged, Cedric?”
{: #nw-v02-c27-p0057 }

“To tell you the truth, I am unable to decide regarding that matter,” Cedric admitted in confidence. “Your hair appears elderly . . . a youthful individual possessing white hair is something I have never encountered. Conversely, the moment you laugh, your eyes possess the exact same youthfulness as those of my lovely instructor. I will share a thought with you, Miss Rosalind” . . . the expression and tone of Cedric matched the gravity of a judge . . . “in my opinion, you possess the qualities to be a magnificent mother. The expression within your eyes is precisely correct . . . it is the very look that was constantly present in my own dear mother’s eyes. It seems unfortunate to me that you do not possess any sons of your own.”
{: #nw-v02-c27-p0058 }

“Cedric, I harbor a small dream boy.”
{: #nw-v02-c27-p0059 }

“Oh, is that truly so? What is his age?”
{: #nw-v02-c27-p0060 }

“I believe he is roughly your age. Since my dreams of him began well before your birth, he should logically be your senior. However, I will refuse to allow his age to exceed eleven or twelve, for if I permitted that, he could eventually become a full adult, causing me to lose him.”
{: #nw-v02-c27-p0061 }

“I know,” Cedric nodded. “The wonderful thing about dream-people is that . . . they remain whatever age you desire them to be. The only individuals in existence that I am aware of who possess dream-people are you, my gorgeous teacher, and I. Is it not peculiar and pleasant that we all happen to be acquainted? However, I suppose those sorts of folks invariably discover one another. Dream-people are something Grandma never possesses, and Mary Joe believes my mind is touched due to my having them. Yet having them seems marvelous to me. You understand, Miss Rosalind. Relate to me everything concerning your small dream-boy.”
{: #nw-v02-c27-p0062 }

“His eyes are blue and his hair is curly. Every morning, he sneaks in to wake me with a kiss. After that, he spends the whole day playing here in the garden . . . and I join in his play. The games we play are wonderful. We race each other and converse with the echoes; and I recount stories to him. And as twilight approaches . . .”
{: #nw-v02-c27-p0063 }

“I know,” Cedric eagerly cut in. “He arrives and places himself next to you . . . like this . . . since naturally at twelve years old he would be overly large for sitting in your lap . . . and rests his head against your shoulder . . . like this . . . and your arms encircle him to grasp him very, very closely, resting your cheek upon his head . . . yes, it happens precisely like that. Oh, you certainly understand, Miss Rosalind.”
{: #nw-v02-c27-p0064 }

When Nell emerged from the stone house, she discovered the pair of them in that spot, and an expression on Miss Rosalind’s face caused her to feel reluctant to interrupt them.
{: #nw-v02-c27-p0065 }

“We ought to leave, Cedric, if our goal is to reach home prior to nightfall, I fear. Miss Rosalind, I plan to self-invite to Echo Cottage for an entire week in the near future.”
{: #nw-v02-c27-p0066 }

“I will retain you for a fortnight if you visit for seven days,” warned Miss Rosalind.
{: #nw-v02-c27-p0067 }
